curiosity: How can adding an extra dark filter between two crossed polarizers make light suddenly reappear?

titles.desktop: The Quantum Mystery of Light: The 3-Filter Polarization Paradox

desktop_mission.mission_sub: Malus's Law, Vector Field Projections & Quantum Measurement
desktop_mission.voice_mission: Today we're simulating Malus's law and the three-filter polarization paradox in Kotlin.
math_cards: Transmitted light intensity drops with the square of the angle between polarization axes
Electric field vectors project along each filter transmission axis in sequence
Adding a 45° diagonal filter restores 12.5% light from complete crossed darkness
desktop_mission.voice_math: The core physics: Malus's law, sequential electric field vector projection, and quantum state rotation.

math_steps.note: Unpolarized light loses half its power; second filter projects the surviving electric field
math_steps.code:
// 1. Initial polarization and first interface Malus transmission
val i1 = 0.5f * inputIntensity
val deltaTheta12Rad = (theta2Deg - theta1Deg) * PI.toFloat() / 180f
val i2 = if (filter2Active) i1 * cos(deltaTheta12Rad).pow(2) else i1
math_steps.sub_desc: Computes initial unpolarized transmission and middle filter electric field projection.

math_steps.note: Light emerging from filter 2 is rotated to θ_2, giving it a non-zero projection onto filter 3
math_steps.sub_desc: Applies final projection through horizontal analyzer filter.

math_steps.note: Adding the middle 45° filter paradoxically increases total transmitted light from 0% to 12.5%
math_steps.code:
// 3. Peak 3-filter paradox transmission at 45 degree angle
val transmittedFraction = i3 / inputIntensity
val isParadoxActive = filter2Active && abs(theta3Deg - theta1Deg - 90f) < 2f && transmittedFraction > 0.001f
val eFieldAmp = sqrt(transmittedFraction)
math_steps.sub_desc: Evaluates paradox state condition and transmitted electric field amplitude.

mystery.en: Why does adding a third dark polarizing filter between two crossed filters cause light to reappear?

en.title: Polarization & The 3-Filter Paradox
en.teaser: Two crossed 90° polarizing sheets block 100% of light; inserting a 45° filter between them restores 12.5% transmission.

en.hook: How can adding another dark sunglasses filter between two crossed lenses make light suddenly reappear?
en.math: The middle filter rotates the light's electric field vector to 45 degrees, giving it a non-zero projection onto the final horizontal analyzer.
en.question: Can we simulate Malus's law and the 3-filter paradox live in Kotlin Multiplatform?
en.code_tip: We project electric field amplitudes through each filter interface and evaluate transmitted Poynting flux on Canvas.
en.payoff: The 3-filter polarization paradox running live in Kotlin.
